title: A gate that runs beside live workers returns verdicts about the machine, not the tree
description:
First widened run of epic-9pd, 2026-09-17. bzx's integrated gate ran while three workers (oe0, pbb, q1e) were still thinking in their own worktrees. Every package took two to four times its usual wall clock - internal/reconcile 848s against 388s on a quiet machine, internal/runstate 601s against 164s - and one timing-sensitive test failed: TestALaunchPastTheCallBoundProducesNoVerdictAndNoTeardown in internal/exec/herdr.

bzx's own change touched internal/cli and nothing else. It was refused for a test in a package it never went near, because the run's own concurrency had saturated the machine. That is a verdict about the machine wearing a verdict's clothes.

Two fixes, one done: the specific test sampled a race it had set up itself (herdr completes the launch at 800ms, the client gives up at 300ms) and won it only while the machine was idle; it now waits for the spawn with a deadline. The systemic half is open. The gate declares -parallel 12, which assumes an idle host; at width N it is competing with N-1 agents and whatever they compile and test. Candidate shapes: derive the gate's parallelism from the width, quiesce dispatch while a gate runs, or give the gate a machine of its own (which is what Phase 4's cloud host would do for free).

Also worth a sweep: this is unlikely to be the only load-sensitive test, and each one is a tick refused at random until it is found.
notes:
2026-09-17 23:58 - The gate's resource envelope is a MEMORY problem as well as a CPU one, and it is now hitting the orchestrator itself.

During epic-9pd's gates the system went low on memory twice, and each time the harness killed the operator's watcher as collateral - the run was never in trouble, but the thing watching it died. 'go test -parallel 12' spawns twelve test binaries at once; on this host that is enough to trigger the memory guard.

Two consequences worth designing for, not just the slowness already recorded here:
- A gate can kill things that are not the gate. Anything sharing the host - the watcher, another agent, the operator's editor - is a candidate victim.
- The failure is silent from the run's point of view. The run kept going and never knew its observer was gone, which is the stall shape this project keeps rediscovering: the orchestration was fine, the monitoring died.

Mitigation taken now: the watcher was rewritten leaner (no python per poll, 120s beat) and relaunched. That treats the symptom. The fix belongs here - the gate's parallelism should account for the host it shares, whether that means deriving it from the width, quiescing while gating, or Phase 4's separate machine.
2026-09-18 06:53 - Fourth load-sensitive test found, same pattern, same cost.

TestAReleaseNeverRecordsTheOperatorIdentity (internal/reconcile/settle_identity_test.go) kills a supervisor then immediately asks a fresh reconciler to release the attempt. Settle refuses a live attempt by design, so the test depends on the kill landing before the next probe - true on an idle machine, false under gate load. It refused tick sqx, whose change touched close-out CI gating and nothing near attempt liveness. Fixed by waiting for the precondition rather than sampling it.

The four so far: TestALaunchPastTheCallBoundProducesNoVerdictAndNoTeardown (herdr, refused bzx), TestTheStallWarningChangesNoVerdict (reconcile, refused 7zs), TestFactoryDeployAndSetupAreWired (cli, hung 45m on a wedged docker daemon and refused oe0), and this one. Every one of them refused a tick whose own change was somewhere else entirely.

That is the cost this tick is really about: not that gates are slow, but that a slow gate REFUSES INNOCENT WORK, and each refusal costs an hour-long re-gate to discover it was nothing. A sweep for the remaining ones is worth more than it sounds.
2026-09-18 07:56 - Fifth: TestAPendingCIThatNeverConcludesIsBounded (sqx's own test). Its 200ms GateTimeout bounded the fixture's gate COMMAND as well as the CI wait; the command exceeded 200ms under load and the test reported a gate error for tick a2 instead of the CI refusal it asserts. Worked around at f436737; the underlying conflation of two bounds is filed as 8kz.

Five for five, every one refusing a tick whose change was elsewhere: bzx, 7zs, oe0, sqx (twice). The run has now spent more wall time re-gating innocent work than the work itself took.
acceptance_criteria: A gate's verdict does not change with the number of workers running beside it: the same tree gates the same way at width 1 and width 4. Either the gate's resource envelope accounts for the run's width, or the run does not gate while it holds live attempts. The repository's timing-sensitive tests are identified and made to wait for conditions rather than sample them.
